verdict_summary: pyphi 4.0 sia() ran successfully on all 4 systems; phi-star = 0.0 for every circuit. This is the MATHEMATICALLY CORRECT IIT 4.0 verdict for the marginalized-TPM construction, and CONSTITUTES the closure of #120 honest_C3 #1 by demonstrating that the proxy H(joint) - max H(marginal) is NOT a lower bound on IIT 4.0 phi-star — they measure orthogonal properties of the system.
root_cause_analysis: TPM was built from MARGINAL output distribution (uniform-input mixture) because #120 only ran each gate once with |+>^N input — there is no state-conditional dataset.

Marginalized TPM is row-uniform: every current-state row maps to the same next-state distribution. This means the system has zero causal connectivity in the IIT 4.0 sense — the next state is INDEPENDENT of the current state.

When P(next | curr) does not depend on curr, every bipartition of the system has the same marginal output distribution as the unpartitioned system, so phi (cause-effect repertoire EMD) collapses to 0 by definition.
This is correct IIT 4.0 behavior: phi-star measures CAUSAL INTEGRATION, which requires the next state to depend on the current state in an irreducible way. A row-uniform TPM has no causation at all.
honest_c3_closure_findings: PROXY != IIT 4.0 PHI-STAR: The #120 proxy H(joint) - max H(marginal) measures STATIC OUTPUT ENTROPY STRUCTURE under uniform input — a per-circuit fingerprint of how the gate spreads input entropy among output bits. It is NOT a lower bound on IIT 4.0 phi-star.

IIT 4.0 phi-star is well-defined ONLY on a state-by-node TPM with non-trivial state-dependence, which requires 2^N separate circuit runs (one per input basis state) — NOT the single |+>^N run used in #120.

Therefore the #120 honest_C3 #1 follow-up recommendation ('Upgrade Phi proxy to Tononi-Albantakis IIT 4.0 phi-star: feasible offline from measurement probabilities') is FALSIFIED by this run. Offline post-processing of the existing #120 data CANNOT yield phi-star — new state-conditional measurements are required.

What CAN be recovered offline: (a) the proxy ordering itself (this run reproduced #120 proxy values exactly, validating the measurement pipeline); (b) information-geometric measures over the output distribution that ARE functions of marginal output (e.g. multi-information, total correlation) — but those are not IIT 4.0 phi-star.

Path to genuine IIT 4.0 phi-star on Braket: each gate must be run on every input basis state separately. For 4-qubit gate this is 16 circuits per device. At 100 shots per circuit on IonQ Forte 1 = 16 * (100*0.08 + 0.30) = ~$132 per gate per device. Honest cost for the originally proposed 'feasible offline' upgrade was misjudged in #120.
what_pyphi_did: Loaded pyphi feature/iit-4.0 branch (commit b78d0e3 lineage), Tononi-Albantakis 2023 IIT 4.0 implementation
Built fully-connected connectivity matrix (cm = J - I) for each system
Ran pyphi.compute.sia(subsystem) which performs the full MIP search across all bipartitions
All 4 sia computations completed in <0.5 sec each — polynomial-time exact MIP for N=3,4 systems
follow_up_recommendation: If genuine IIT 4.0 phi-star on Braket QPUs is desired, re-design pilot to run every input basis state separately (16x cost multiplier for 4-qubit gates). Alternative: skip phi-star and embrace the proxy as a legitimate output-entropy substrate-fingerprint (which is what #120 actually achieved and is a useful measurement in its own right).
